answer: The relic multiplier is published, charged in onyx, and anchor lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 3224 identities would post 2980 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
